# hyperv_ics_network (Resource)

**Requirements:** the Host Network Service (`hns`) must be present. On Windows Server, enable it with `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Containers-HNS -All` and restart the host. Tested with the built-in `Administrator` account on Windows Server 2022 (build 10.0.20348); a less privileged identity hasn't been tested.

Manages one [Host Compute Network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/api/hcn/hns_schema) of type `ICS`. Guests on it get a DHCP lease, DNS, and outbound NAT through the host, and the host itself takes `host_address`, the first address in `address_prefix`. The network persists across host reboots with the same ID, prefix, and isolation ID.

Every ICS network on a host shares one Internal `VMSwitch`. The first ICS network creates it and names it after itself, and the switch keeps that name after that network is deleted. Deleting the last ICS network removes the switch. HNS also assigns each network a VLAN isolation ID, and a guest NIC gets a lease only when its isolation ID matches. Connect a VM by setting `hyperv_vm.network_adapter[*].switch_name` to `switch_name` and `hyperv_vm.network_adapter[*].isolation_id` to `isolation_id`.

A guest can get a different lease after a host reboot. Read its address from `hyperv_vm.<x>.network_adapter[0].ip_addresses` rather than hard-coding it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A NAT'd subnet with DHCP and DNS from the host. The host takes 172.30.97.1.
resource "hyperv_ics_network" "lab" {
  name           = "lab"
  address_prefix = "172.30.97.0/24"
}

# A guest NIC gets a lease only when its isolation ID matches the network's.
resource "hyperv_vm" "node" {
  name       = "node"
  generation = 2
  cpu        = { count = 2 }
  memory     = { startup_bytes = 4294967296 }

  network_adapter = [
    {
      name         = "primary"
      switch_name  = hyperv_ics_network.lab.switch_name
      isolation_id = hyperv_ics_network.lab.isolation_id
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address_prefix` (String) IPv4 subnet in CIDR notation, such as `172.30.97.0/24`. The address must be the network address and the prefix `/30` or shorter. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `name` (String) Network name, unique among the host's HCN networks. It also names the host vNIC, `vEthernet (<name>)`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `host_address` (String) Host's address on the network, the first address in `address_prefix`. Guests use it as their gateway and DNS server.
- `id` (String) HCN network GUID.
- `isolation_id` (Number) VLAN isolation ID HNS assigned to this network. A guest NIC needs the same value in `hyperv_vm.network_adapter[*].isolation_id` to get a lease.
- `switch_name` (String) Name of the Internal `VMSwitch` every ICS network on the host shares. Attach guest NICs to this switch.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an ICS network by its HCN network GUID.
terraform import hyperv_ics_network.example "753900d5-83fd-4c4d-83b6-7c438c6ff4fe"
```
